Commercial precision-ag platforms show inconsistent results with NDVI-based variable-rate nitrogen application, often failing to achieve promised nitrogen savings while sometimes causing yield penalties in certain soil types and weather conditions

The claimed 10-15% nitrogen reduction is not consistently supported by evidence, with multiple studies showing no significant difference between NDVI-based variable-rate application and uniform application when properly accounting for application costs and calibration requirements

The system requires prohibitively expensive infrastructure including high-resolution satellite/drone imaging, specialized software, and calibrated variable-rate spreaders that cannot be economically justified for most farming operations

NDVI values are confounded by multiple factors including soil moisture, crop residue, weed pressure, and atmospheric conditions, creating measurement noise that overwhells the nitrogen status signal and leads to misclassification of management zones
